chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man said to him: 'I set out for Mecca and a man accompanied me, and he was my companion. When we were on part of the journey, he fell ill and became severely weak. I would attend to him, then he regained consciousness until there was no harm to him in my view. When it was the day on which he died, he regained consciousness and then died on that day.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no dead person whose death approaches but that Allah, Exalted and Mighty, returns to him from his hearing, sight, and intellect [the faculty] for the will. He takes the will or leaves it. And it is the ease/repose which is called the 'repose of death'. So it is a right upon every Muslim.'

key_terms.رَاحَةُ الْمَوْتِ: Repose of death (final period of clarity before death)

ai.seo_question: What is the 'repose of death' and why is making a will obligatory for Muslims?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the physiological and spiritual phenomenon of *rahat al-mawt*, where Allah restores a dying person's faculties to ensure they fulfill the obligation of bequeathing. This specific clarity serves as a final opportunity for spiritual accounting, reinforcing the juristic consensus that making a will is a mandatory right (*haqq*) upon every Muslim, whether they possess wealth or not.
